translations.text: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
As it is written in Isaiah the prophet: "Behold, I will send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your ways before you."
"The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the ways of the Lord and make his paths straight."
John was in the wilderness, baptizing and preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins.
And all the region of Judea and all the people of Jerusalem went out to him, and they were all baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
And John was clothed in a garment of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist, and he ate locusts and wild honey.
He preached and said: "Behold, one mightier than I is coming after me, the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to untie.
I baptize you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit."
And it came to pass in those days that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
And immediately, as he came up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened and the Spirit of God descending upon him like a dove.
And a voice came from heaven: "You are my beloved Son; in you I am well pleased."
And immediately the Spirit led him out into the wilderness.
And he was there forty days, being tempted by the devil, and he was with the wild beasts, and the angels ministered to him.
And after John was handed over, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Gospel of the kingdom of God,
and saying: "The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has drawn near; repent and believe in the Gospel."
And as he was passing by the Sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting nets into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And Jesus said to them: "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men."
And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
And going on a little farther, he saw James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, and they were mending the nets in the boat.
And he called them. And immediately they left Zebedee their father in the boat with his hired workers and followed him.
And they went into Capernaum. And immediately on the Sabbath day he entered their synagogue and taught them.
And the people were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as one who has authority, and not as their scribes.
And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out
and said: "Ah, what have we to do with you, Jesus of Nazareth? You have come to destroy us. We know who you are, the Holy One of God."
Jesus rebuked him and said: "Be silent, and come out of him!"
And the unclean spirit threw him down, and cried out with a loud voice, and went out of him.
And all were amazed, so much that they questioned one another and said: "What is this new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him."
And the report about him went out through all the region of Galilee.
And he went out from the synagogue and came to the house of Simon and Andrew, with John and James.
Now Simon's mother-in-law lay sick with a fever. And they told Jesus about her.
And he came and took her by the hand and raised her up; and the fever left her, and she got up and served them.
And when evening came and the sun was setting, they brought to him all the sick and those possessed by demons.
And the whole city was gathered before the door.
And he healed all of them of evil diseases and of various kinds of sicknesses, and he cast out many demons; and he did not allow the demons to speak, for they knew him, that he was the Christ.
And at daybreak, very early while it was barely dawn, he got up and went out from there, and went away to a desert place, and there he prayed.
And Simon and those who were with him followed after him.
And they found him and said to him: "Everyone is looking for you."
But Jesus said to them: "Come, let us go to the nearby villages and towns, so that I may preach there, for it is for this that I was sent."
And he preached in their synagogues and throughout all Galilee, and cast out demons.
Then a leper came to him, pleading with him; and he knelt down and said to him: "Lord, if you will, you are able to make me clean."
And Jesus had pity on him, and stretched out his hand and touched him and said to him: "I will; be clean!"
And as soon as he said this, the leprosy immediately left him, and he was made clean.
And he spoke sternly to him and immediately sent him away.
And he said to him: "See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest and offer for your cleansing what Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."

But he went out from there and began to proclaim it widely and to spread the word around, so that he could no longer openly enter a city, but stayed outside in desert places. And people came to him from every side.
And he entered Capernaum again, and after a few days it was heard that he was in the house.
And a multitude of people gathered there, until there was no longer room even in front of the doors, and he spoke the word to them.
And they came to him bringing a paralyzed man, carried aloft by four men.
And since they could not get near him because of the crowd, they stripped off the roof of the house where he was, and they lifted up and let down the bed on which the paralytic lay.
And Jesus saw their faith and said to the paralytic: "Child, your sins are forgiven you!"
Some of the scribes were sitting there, and they reasoned in their hearts and said,
"This man is speaking blasphemy. Who has the power to forgive sins but God alone?"
But Jesus perceived in his spirit that they were reasoning this way in their hearts, and he said to them: "Why do you reason so in your hearts?
Which is easier: to say to this paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven you,' or to say, 'Rise, take up your bed and walk'?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins" — he said to the paralysed man,
I say to you: Rise, take up your bed and go to your house!"
And he rose immediately, took up the bed and went out in front of everyone, so that all were amazed and glorified God, saying: "We have never seen anything like this."
And he went out again to the seashore, and all the people followed him, and there he taught them.
And going on from there he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus as he sat at the tax booth, and he said to him: "Follow me!" And he rose and followed him.
And it happened that as he sat in his house, many tax collectors and sinners were sitting with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many there and they were following him.
And when the scribes and the Pharisees saw him, that he was eating with tax collectors and sinners, they said to his disciples: "Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
And Jesus heard this and said to them, "Those who are healthy do not need a physician, but those who are sick. I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance."
And the disciples of John and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came to him and said to him: "Why do the disciples of John and those of the Pharisees fast, and your disciples do not fast?"
Jesus said to them: "The sons of the bridegroom cannot fast as long as the bridegroom is with them.
But days will come when the bridegroom will be lifted up from them, and then they will fast, in those days.
No one puts a new patch on an old garment; otherwise the fresh new patch tears away from the old, and the tear becomes worse.
And no one pours new wine into an old wineskin, so that the new wine may not burst the wineskin, and the wine be spilled, and the wineskins be ruined; rather, new wine is poured into new wineskins."
And it happened that he was passing through the grainfields on the Sabbath, and his disciples began to walk along the way and to pluck the heads of grain.
And the Pharisees said to him: "See what your disciples are doing on the Sabbath, which is not lawful to do!"
And Jesus said to them, "Have you never read what David did when he was in need and he and those with him were hungry?

how he entered the house of God in the time of Abiathar the high priest and ate the loaves of offering, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone, and gave them also to those who were with him.
And he said to them, "The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath.
Therefore the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.
And again he entered the synagogue. And there was a man there whose hand was withered.
And they were watching him to see whether he would heal him on the sabbath, so that they might accuse him.
At that time Jesus said to the man whose hand was withered: Get up and come forward into the middle!
And Jesus said to them: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil? To save a life or to destroy it? But they kept silent.

And he looked around at them with anger, grieved at the blindness of their heart, and said to the man: Stretch out your hand! And he stretched out his hand, and that hand was restored, just like the other one.
And when the Pharisees went out from there with the Herodians, they plotted against him, how they might destroy him.
But Jesus with his disciples withdrew from them and came to the sea, and a large crowd from Galilee and from Judea,
and from Jerusalem and from beyond the Jordan, and those from the region of Tyre and from Sidon. A great multitude heard how much he was doing, and they came to him.
And he told his disciples to prepare a boat for him because of the crowd, so that they would not press up against him and crowd him.
For he was healing many, so that the crowd kept pressing in on him just to touch him. And as many as had illnesses and touched him were healed.
And when the unclean spirits saw him, they fell down before him, crying out and saying: "You are the Son of God."
And he sternly warned them not to make him known.
And he went up on the mountain and called to him those he wanted; and they came to him.
And he appointed the Twelve, so that they would be with him, and he sent them out to preach,
And they were to have authority to cast out demons.
And he gave the name Peter to Simon,
and James son of Zebedee and John, the brother of James; and he gave them the names Boanerges, which means: sons of thunder;
and Andrew and Philip, Bartholomew and Matthew the tax collector, and Thomas and James son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus and Simon the Canaanite
and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And they came to a house, and the crowd gathered to him again, and they were not even able to eat bread.
And those close to him heard and came out to seize him, for they were saying: He is out of his mind.
And the scribes who had come down from Jerusalem were saying: Beelzebul is with him, and by the prince of demons he casts out demons.
And he called them to him and spoke to them in parables: How can a demon cast out a demon?
And if a kingdom is divided against a kingdom, that kingdom cannot stand firm.
And if a house is divided against a house, that house cannot stand firm.
And if the devil has risen up against himself and is divided, he cannot stand, but he comes to an end.
And no one can enter the house of a strong man and plunder his goods unless he first binds the strong man, and then he may plunder his house.
Amen I say to you that all sins and blasphemies will be forgiven the sons of men, however much they may blaspheme;
but whoever speaks blasphemy against the Holy Spirit has no forgiveness, but is liable to eternal judgment.
For they were saying: An unclean spirit is with him.
And his brothers and his mother came, and they stood outside and sent to him and were calling him.
And a crowd was sitting around him; and when they said to him: Behold, your mother and your brothers are standing outside and are looking for you,
Jesus answered them and said to them: Who is my mother, or who are my brothers?
And he looked around at his disciples sitting about him and said: Behold, my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of God, this one is my brother and my sister and my mother."
Then again he began to teach by the seashore; and a great crowd gathered to him, so that he got into a boat, and he sat in the boat on the sea; and all the crowd stood on the land by the seashore.
And he taught them many things in parables, and said to them in his teaching:
"Listen to this: A sower went out to sow.
And it happened as he sowed that some fell on the road, and the birds came and ate it.
And other seed fell on rocky ground, where there was not much soil, and it sprang up immediately, because there was no depth of soil.
And when the sun rose, it was scorched, and because it had not put down roots, it withered.
And other seed fell among thorns; and the thorns sprang up and choked it, and it did not bear fruit.
And other seed fell on good ground and gave fruit, coming up and growing, and it brought forth thirtyfold, sixtyfold, and a hundredfold."
And he said: "Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!"
And when he was alone, his disciples asked him: What is this parable?
And he said to them: "To you it has been given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, but to those outside everything is spoken in parables,
So that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they should turn back and be forgiven.
And he said to them: Do you not know this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
The one who sows sows the word.
And these are the ones on the road, where the word is sown; and whenever they hear his word, the devil comes and takes away from them the word that was sown in them.
And these are the ones sown on the rocky ground: when they hear the word, they receive it at once with joy,
And they have no root in themselves, but are temporary; and when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, they immediately stumble.
And those that were sown among the thorns are the ones who hear the word,
and the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of riches enter in and choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And these are the ones that were sown on good ground: those who hear the word and receive it and bear fruit, thirtyfold and sixtyfold and a hundredfold.
And he said to them: "Is a lamp brought in to be put under a bushel, or set under a bed? Is it not set on a lampstand?
For there is nothing hidden that will not be revealed, nor is there any secret except that it may come into the open.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And he said to them: "Take heed what you hear. With the measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be added to you who hear.
Whoever has, to him it will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken from him.
And he said to them: The kingdom of God is like this: as when a man sows seed in the ground
and sleeps; and he rises night and day, and the seed sprouts and grows, in a way that he does not know,
for of itself the earth brings forth fruit: first the blade, then the head, and then the full wheat in the head.
And when it yields its fruit, he immediately sends in the sickle, for the harvest has come.
And he said: To what shall we compare the kingdom of God? Or what parable shall we offer for it?
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the ground, is smaller than all the seeds that are on the earth.
And when it is sown, it comes up and becomes greater than all the herbs and puts forth very large branches, so that the birds of the sky can settle beneath its shade.
And with many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
And without a parable he said nothing to them; but privately he would explain everything to the disciples.
On that day, when evening had come, he said to them: "Let us cross over to the other side."
And the disciples left the crowd and took him with them, just as he was in the boat, and there were other boats too that were with him.
And at once there arose a great storm of wind, and it was driving the waves into the boat, so that the boat was even filling up.
And he himself was at the end of the boat, asleep. And they woke him and said to him: "Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?"
And he rose and rebuked the wind and the sea and said: Be silent and shut your mouth! And the wind abated, and there was a great calm.
And he said to them: "Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?"
And they were afraid with great fear and said to one another: "Who then is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
And he came across the sea, to the country of the Gergesenes.
And as he came out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit came from the tombs to meet him,
He had his dwelling among the tombs, and no one was able to bind him, not even with chains.
For many times he had been bound with chains and fetters, and he would break them apart and shatter them, and no one could restrain him.
And always, night and day, he would roam about the tombs and the mountains, crying out and cutting himself with stones.
And when he saw Jesus from afar, he came running and worshiped him,
crying out with a loud voice and saying: "What is there between you and me and you [?], Jesus, Son of God Most High? I adjure you by God, do not torment me."
For Jesus was saying to him: You unclean spirit, come out of that man!
And he asked him: "What is your name?" And he said to him: "My name is Legion, for we are many."
And they begged him earnestly not to drive them out of the country.
And there was a great herd of swine there, feeding on the mountainside.
And all the demons begged him, saying: Send us to those swine, so that we may enter into them.

And he commanded them, and the unclean spirits came out of the man and entered the swine, and the herd of swine rushed down the steep bank into the sea, for they were about two thousand, and they were drowned in the sea.
But their herdsmen fled and told it in the city and the villages. And people came out to see what it was that had happened.
And they came to Jesus and saw the demon-possessed man, the one in whom the Legion had been, sitting clothed and in his right mind, and they were afraid.
And those who had seen it told them how it had happened to the demoniac, and about the swine.
And they began to beg him to depart from their borders.
And as Jesus was getting into the boat, the man who had formerly been demon-possessed begged him that he might be with him.
And he did not permit him, but said to him: "Go to your home, to your own people, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you and how he has had mercy on you."
And he went away and began to proclaim in the Decapolis how much Jesus had done for him; and everyone marveled.
And when Jesus had crossed over again to the other side, a great crowd gathered to him. And he was by the seashore,
and behold, a certain ruler of the synagogue came to him, whose name was Jairus; and he saw him and fell at his feet.
And he begged him earnestly, saying: "My daughter is dying; come and lay your hands on her, that she may be saved and live."
And Jesus went with him. And a great crowd followed him and pressed upon him.
And there was a woman there who had been afflicted with a flow of blood for twelve years.
She had suffered greatly at the hands of many physicians and had spent all that she had, and it had brought her no benefit, but rather she had grown worse.
And when she heard about Jesus, she came up to him from behind in the crowd and touched his garment,
for she said in her heart: "If I touch even just his garment, I shall be healed."
And as soon as she touched it, the flow of her blood immediately dried up, and she knew in her body that she was healed of the affliction.
But Jesus, perceiving in himself that power had gone out from him, turned to the crowd and said: "Who touched my garment?"
But his disciples said to him: "You see this crowd pressing upon you, and you say: 'Who touched me?'"
And he looked around to see the one who had done this.
But the woman was afraid and trembled, knowing what had happened to her; she came and fell down before him and told him the whole cause of it.
And he said to her: "Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go to your home in peace, and be alive and free of your affliction!"
And while he was saying this, people from the synagogue ruler's house came and said to him: "Your daughter has died. Why trouble the teacher any further?"
But when Jesus heard the words they were saying, he said to the synagogue ruler: "Do not be afraid, only believe!"
And he allowed no one to follow with him except Peter and James and John, the brother of James.
And they came to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and he saw an uproar and weeping and much wailing.
And he went in and said to them: Why are you in an uproar? The child is not dead, but is sleeping.
And they mocked him, but he himself drove out all that uproar, and he took the child's father and mother and his disciples, and he went in where the dead child lay,
and he took the child's hand and said to her: Talitha kumi! Which translated is: I say to you, child, arise!
And immediately the girl arose and began to walk, for she was only twelve years old. And they were utterly overcome with great amazement.
And he strictly charged them that no one should learn of this, and he ordered them to give her food.
And he went out from there and came to his own home town, and his disciples followed him.

And it was the Sabbath, and he began to teach them in their synagogue. And many who heard him were astonished and said: Where did this man get this? And what is this wisdom given to him, and such great powers that are done by his hands?
Is this not the carpenter's son and the son of Mary, the brother of James and Joses, Judas and Simon, and are not all his sisters with us? And they stumbled over him.
But Jesus said to them: "A prophet is not without honor except in his own country, among his own kin, and in his own house."
And he did no mighty work there, not a single one, except that he laid his hand on a few sick people and healed them.
And he marveled at their unbelief, and Jesus went around the surrounding villages and taught them.
And he called the twelve to him and began to send them out two by two, and he gave them authority over unclean spirits.
And he commanded them to take nothing for the road except a staff only: no bags, no bread, no copper money in their belts.
And that they should wear sandals, and not put on two garments.
And he said to them: "Whatever house you enter, stay there until you leave that place."
And as many as do not receive you and do not listen to you, when you go out from there, shake the dust off your feet as a testimony to them.
And they went out and preached that people should repent.
And they cast out many demons, and anointed many sick people with oil and healed them.
And King Herod heard, for his name had become known, and they were saying: John the Baptist has risen from the dead, and because of this powers are at work in him.
And others were saying: He is a prophet, or one of the former prophets.
When Herod heard, he said: John, whom I beheaded, he has risen.
For this Herod had sent and arrested John, put him in fetters and placed him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother, for he had taken her as his wife.
And John said to Herod: It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife as your wife.
But Herodias held it in her heart against him and wanted to kill him, and she could do nothing.
For Herod feared John and knew that he was a righteous and holy man, and he guarded him and would listen to him, and he showed him much honor and listened to him fittingly.
And when an opportune day came, when Herod, at the time of his birthday, prepared a supper for his chief men and his centurions and the nobles of Galilee,
the daughter of Herodias came in and danced; and she pleased Herod and those reclining at table with him. And King Herod said to the girl: Ask me for whatever you wish, and I will give it to you,
up to half of my kingdom.
And she went out and asked her mother: "What shall I ask for?" And she said to her: "The head of John the Baptist."
And the girl went in quickly to the king and said: I want you to give me right now, on a platter, the head of John the Baptist.
And King Herod became sorrowful, but because of his oath and those reclining at table with him he did not wish to slight the girl.
And immediately he sent his swordsman and ordered him to bring his head.
And he went and beheaded him in the prison, and he brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl presented it to her mother.
And his disciples heard of it, and they came and wrapped his body and buried it in a tomb.
And the apostles of Jesus came and gathered around him, and told him everything they had done and taught.
And Jesus said to them: Come away by yourselves to a deserted place and rest a little. For there were many coming and going, and they did not even have time to eat bread.
And they went away by themselves in a boat to a deserted place.
And the people saw them as they were going away, and many understood, and they quickly gathered there from all the cities and came to them.
And Jesus came out and saw a great crowd, and he had compassion on them, for they were like sheep that have no shepherd. And he began to teach them at length.
And when much time had passed, his disciples came to him and said: This place is deserted, and the hour is already very late.
Send this crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding countryside and buy themselves something to eat.
But he answered and said to them: You give them something to eat. And they said to him: Shall we go and buy two hundred drachmas' worth of bread and give these people something to eat?
And Jesus said to them: "How many loaves do you have? Go and see!" And they looked and said: "Five loaves and two fish."
And he commanded them all to sit down, company by company, as at a meal, on the green grass.
And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.

And he took the five loaves and the two fish, and he looked up to heaven and blessed, and he broke the bread and gave it to his disciples to set before them; and he likewise divided the two fish among them all.
They all ate and were satisfied.
And they took up the leftover fragments, twelve baskets full, and also some of the fish.
And those who ate were about five thousand men alone.
And immediately he compelled his disciples to get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side of the sea, to Bethsaida, until he should dismiss the crowd.
And he took leave of them and went up on a mountain to pray.
And when evening came, the boat was still only in the middle of the sea, and he himself was alone on land.

And he saw them, that they were struggling in the boat's progress, for the wind was against them. And only at the fourth watch of the night Jesus came to them, walking on the sea, and he meant to pass by them.
But when they saw him walking on the sea, they thought that it was some apparition, and they cried out.
For they all saw him and were terrified. Immediately he spoke to them and said: Take heart, it is I, do not be afraid!
And he went up with them into the boat, and the wind ceased; and his disciples were all the more astonished.
For they had not understood about the loaves, because their hearts were dulled.
And they crossed over and came to the land of Gennesaret.
And as soon as they came out of the boat, the people of that place immediately recognized him.
And they ran about through all that countryside and began to bring all the sick on beds to wherever they heard he was.

And wherever he entered villages and cities and country estates, they would lay their sick in the streets and beg him that they might touch only the hem of his garment, and as many as touched it were healed.
And the Pharisees and some of the scribes who had come from Jerusalem gathered around him.
And they saw some of his disciples eating with defiled hands, that is, with unwashed hands, and they reproached them.
For the Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they wash their hands up to the elbow, for they held to the teaching handed down by the elders.

And when they come in from the streets, if they do not wash, they do not eat; and there are many other things that they have received to observe: the washing of cups and pitchers and cauldrons and beds.
Then the Pharisees and the scribes asked him: Why do your disciples not walk according to the teaching of the elders, but eat bread with defiled hands?
But Jesus answered and said to them: Well did the prophet Isaiah speak about you hypocrites: This people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far removed from me.
In vain they serve me, teaching the teachings and commandments of men.
And you have abandoned the commandment of God and hold to the teaching of men.
And he said to them: "Well do you set aside the commandment of God, so that you may establish your own teaching.
For Moses said: Honor your father and your mother; and whoever speaks evil of father or mother, let him die by death.
But you say: If a man says to his father or mother, "Corban," which is a gift, "whatever benefit you might have had from me" --
then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or mother.
And you have made the word of God void by that teaching of yours which you teach; and you do many things like these."
And he called all the people to him and said to them: Listen to me and understand.
There is nothing going into a man from outside that could defile him; rather, what comes out of him, that is what defiles a man.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear!
And when he had gone into the house away from the people, his disciples asked him about the parable.
And he said to them: Are you also likewise without understanding, and do you not know that nothing entering a man from outside defiles him?
For it does not enter the heart but the belly, and it goes out through the drain, purifying all foods."
And he said: What comes out of a man, that is what defiles a man.
For from within, out of the heart of men, come evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, thefts, murders,
Acts of greed, wickedness, deceit, impurity, evil eyes, blasphemies, arrogance, folly.
All these evil things come out from within, and they defile a man.
And from there he arose and went away to the region of Tyre and Sidon. And he entered a house and did not want anyone to know of it, but he could not be hidden.
For a certain woman, who had a daughter afflicted by an unclean spirit, heard about him, and she came and fell down at his feet.
Now the woman was a Gentile, by race a Syrian of the seacoast, and she begged him to drive the demon out of her daughter.
But Jesus said to her: Let the children be filled first, for it is not good to take bread from the children and throw it to the dogs.
But she answered and said to him: Lord, even the dogs under the table eat from the children's crumbs.
And Jesus said to her: "For that word, go! The demon has gone out of your daughter."
And the woman went away to her house and found that the demon had gone out, and her daughter was clothed and sitting on the bed.
And again he went out from the region of Tyre and Sidon and came to the Sea of Galilee, through the midst of the region of the Decapolis.
And they brought to him a deaf man who spoke with difficulty, and they begged him to lay his hand on him.
And he took him aside from the crowd by himself, and put his fingers to him, and spat into his ears, and touched his tongue,
and he looked up to heaven and said to him: Ephphatha! which means: Be opened!
And immediately his ears were opened, and the bond of his tongue was loosed, and he spoke correctly.
And he commanded them to tell no one; but the more he commanded them, the more they spread it abroad.
And they were astonished all the more and said: He does all things well: he makes the deaf hear and the mute speak.
In those days, again, there was a great crowd, and they had nothing to eat. He called his disciples and said to them:
I have pity on this crowd, for it has been three days that they have been waiting for me, and they have nothing to eat.
And if I send them away fasting to their homes, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come from far away."
And his disciples answered and said to him: How can we fill so many people with bread here in the wilderness?
And he asked them: How many loaves do you have? And they said to him: Seven.
And he commanded the crowd to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves, gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to distribute; and they distributed them to the crowd.
And they also had a few fish, and he blessed those too and commanded them to set them out.
And they ate and were filled; and they took up the remainder of the fragments, seven baskets.
And those who ate it were about four thousand; and he dismissed them.
And Jesus got into a boat with his disciples and went to the region of Magdala.
And the Pharisees came and began to dispute with him, and they asked him for a sign from heaven, testing him.
And he sighed in his spirit and said: "Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you: no sign will be given to this generation."
And he left them, got into the boat again, and went across to the other side.
And the disciples forgot to take bread; they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
And Jesus instructed them, saying: See to it and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of the Herodians.
But they reasoned among themselves and said: We have no bread with us.
And Jesus perceived it and said to them: Why do you reason in your hearts, you of little faith, that you have no bread? Do you not yet understand, and do you not remember, that your eyes are blinded?
You have eyes and do not see, you have ears and do not hear; do you not understand, and do you not remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you take up? And they said to him: Twelve.
And when the seven for the four thousand, how many hampers of fragments did you take up? And they said to him: Seven.
And Jesus said to them: How then do you not understand?
And they came to Bethsaida, and they brought a blind man to him and begged him to lay his hand on him.
And he took his hand and led him outside, and he spat on his eyes and laid his hand on him and asked him what he could see.
And he looked up and said, "I see people like trees walking about."
And then he again placed his hands on his eyes and opened them; and he received his sight and recovered, and he saw everything brightly and clearly.
And he sent him to his home and said: Go to your home; and when you enter the village, tell no one anything in the village.
And Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi, and on the way he questioned his disciples, saying to them: Who do people say that I am?
And they answered and said to him: John the Baptist; and others: Elijah; and some: one of the prophets.
Jesus said to them: And you, what do you say of me, who am I? Peter answered and said to him: You are the Christ.
And he sternly charged them not to tell anyone about him.
And he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer greatly and be treated with contempt by the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed, and on the third day rise again.
And he spoke this word openly; and Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him for this word.
But he turned around and, seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said to him, "Get behind me, devil, for you are not minding the things of God, but the things of men."
And he called the crowd together with his disciples and said to them: Whoever wishes to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
Whoever wishes to save his soul will lose it; and whoever loses himself for my sake or for the sake of the Gospel, he will save it.
What profit is it to a person if he gains this whole world and destroys his own soul?
And what shall a person give in exchange for his soul?

For whoever is ashamed of me and of these words of mine in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.
And he said to them, "Amen, I say to you, there are some of those standing here who will not see the taste of death until they see the kingdom of God coming with power."
And after six days Jesus took Peter and James and John and led them up a high mountain by themselves alone, and he was changed into another form before them.
And his clothing became radiant and exceedingly white, like snow, such as no fuller on earth is able to whiten in that way.
And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were with Jesus and were conversing.
And Peter answered and said to Jesus: "Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents here: one for you, one for Moses and one for Elijah."
For he did not know what he should answer, because they were afraid.
And a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came out of the cloud and said: "This is my beloved Son; listen to him."
And suddenly they looked around and saw no one, but only Jesus with them.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
And they kept that saying to themselves, and they questioned one another: "What is this 'when he rises from the dead'?"
And they questioned him, saying: "How is it that the scribes say that Elijah must come first?"
But he answered and said to them: "Elijah will come first and restore all things; and as it is written of the Son of Man, that he must suffer greatly and be treated with contempt."
But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, as it is written of him."
And he came to his disciples and saw a crowd around them, and scribes were disputing with them.
And immediately the whole crowd saw him and were amazed, and they ran up and greeted him.
And Jesus asked them and said: "What are you disputing with one another?"
And one of the crowd answered and said: "Teacher, I have brought you my son, who has a spirit of muteness.
And wherever it seizes him, it dashes him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and withers away. And I told your disciples that they should heal him, and they could not."
Jesus answered him and said: "O unbelieving generation! How long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me!"
And they brought him to him. And he saw him, and immediately that unclean spirit dashed him down; and when he had fallen to the ground, he rolled about and foamed.
And Jesus asked his father: "How long has it been since this happened to him?" And he said: "From childhood."
And often it has thrown him into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if you can do anything, help us, Lord, and have mercy on us."
But Jesus said to him: "As for what you are able: everything is possible for one who believes."
And immediately the father of the boy cried out and said: "I believe; help my unbelief."
When Jesus saw that the crowd was gathering around him, he rebuked that spirit and said to it: "You mute and deaf spirit, I command you: come out of him and enter him no more!"
And it cried out loudly, and he rolled about, and it came out of him; and he became like a dead man, so that many even said: "He has died."
But Jesus took his hand and raised him up, and he stood up.
And when Jesus had gone into a house, his disciples asked him privately: "Why were we not able to heal him?"
And he said to them: "This kind cannot come out by anything except by prayer and fasting."
And they went out from there and passed through Galilee; and he did not want anyone to know of it.
For he was teaching his disciples and saying to them: "The Son of Man will be given into the hands of men, and they will kill him; and when he has died, on the third day he will rise."
But they did not understand that saying and were afraid to ask him.
And he came to Capernaum. And when he had entered the house, he asked them: What were you disputing among yourselves on the way?
But they were silent, for on the way they had been saying to one another: Which of us is to be the greatest?
And he sat down and called the twelve and said to them: "Whoever of you wants to be first, let him be the least of all and the servant of all."
And he brought a child and set him in their midst, and took him into his arms and said to them:
Whoever receives one of these children for the sake of my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives not me, but the one who sent me.
John answered him and said: Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, one who does not follow us, and we tried to stop him.
But Jesus said: Do not stop him, for there is no one who will do a mighty work in my name and be able to speak evil of us.
"For whoever is not against us is on our side."
For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink for the sake of my name, because you are Christ's, amen I say to you, his reward will not be lost.
And whoever causes one of the little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for him if a donkey's millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.
And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life without a hand than to have two hands and enter Gehenna, the unquenchable fire,
and if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off: it is better for you to enter life lame than to enter Gehenna with two feet.
And if your eye leads you astray, pluck it out: it is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna.
"where their worm never comes to an end, and the fire is not quenched."
For everyone will be salted with fire.
Salt is good; if salt becomes insipid, with what will it be salted? Have salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.
And Jesus got up and left that place and came to the region of Judea beyond the Jordan. The crowds gathered to him again, and he taught them again, as was his custom.
And the Pharisees came to him and asked him: "Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?" They were testing him.
But he answered and said to them: "What did Moses command you?"
But they said to him: Moses commanded that a bill of divorce be given and that she be sent away.
Jesus answered and said to them: "Because of your hardness of heart Moses wrote that commandment."
"But from the beginning of creation God made them male and female, and said:"
For this reason a man shall leave his father and his mother and cleave to his wife,
and the two shall be one flesh, so that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
Those whom God has joined together, let no man separate.
And afterward, when he was in the house, the disciples asked him again about this same matter.
But Jesus said to them: If a husband sends away his wife and marries another, he has committed adultery.
"And if a wife goes away from her husband and is married to another, she too has committed adultery."
And they were bringing children to him, so that he might lay his hand on them; but the disciples were hindering those who were bringing them.
When Jesus saw it, he was angry with them and said: Let these children come to me and do not stop them, for of such as these is the kingdom of heaven.
Amen I say to you: whoever does not receive the kingdom of God as a child will not enter it.
And he embraced them and laid his hands on them and blessed them.

And as he set out on the way, behold, a certain rich man came running to him and knelt before him, and he implored him and said to him: Good teacher, what deed shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?
But Jesus said to him: Why do you call me good? No one is good except God alone.
You know the commandments: Do not kill, do not steal, do not bear false witness, honor your father and your mother."
And he answered and said to him: "All these I have done from my youth; what do I still lack?"

And Jesus looked at him and loved him, and said to him: If you wish to be perfect, one thing you still lack: go and sell all that you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; come and follow me.
But he was distressed at this word and went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.
And Jesus looked around and said to his disciples: Amen, I say to you that those who have wealth will enter the kingdom of God with difficulty.
But the disciples were astonished at that saying. And Jesus answered again and said to them: Children, how hard it is for those who put their hope in wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
It is easier for the rope of a machine to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
But they were astonished all the more and said to one another: Then who can be saved?
Jesus looked at them and said: With men this is impossible, but not with God, for all things are possible with God.
Peter began to speak to him and said: Behold, we have left everything and have joined ourselves to you.

Jesus answered and said to them: "Amen, I say to you: there is no one who has left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for my sake and for the sake of this gospel
[?] unless he receives a hundredfold now, in this time: house and brothers and sisters, and mother and children and fields, after persecution, and in the age to come eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last first."

And they were on the road, going up to Jerusalem; and Jesus was going ahead of them, and the disciples were astonished. And they followed him and were afraid to question him. And he again took the twelve aside and began to tell them what was to come, what was going to happen to him:
For behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death and hand him over to the Gentiles,
and they will mock him and torment him and spit on him and kill him, and on the third day he will rise.
And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, came to him and said to him: Teacher, we want you to do for us whatever we ask of you.
And he said to them: What do you want from me, that I should do for you?
And they said to him: Grant us that we may sit, one at your right and one at your left, on that day of glory.
And Jesus said to them: You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink, and to be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized?
And they said to him: We are able. Jesus answered and said to them: The cup that I drink you will indeed drink, and with the baptism with which I am baptized you will be baptized,
but to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give; rather, it is for those for whom it has been prepared.
And when the ten heard this, they began to be angry with James and John.
But Jesus called them and said to them: "You know that those who are regarded as rulers of the gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
But it shall not be so among you; rather, whoever wishes to be great among you shall be your servant;
and whoever wishes to be first among you shall be the slave of all.
for indeed the Son of Man did not come to be served by anyone, but to serve and to give his soul as a ransom for many.
And they came to Jericho. And as Jesus and his disciples were going out of Jericho, with a great crowd, the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind man, was sitting by the road as a beggar.
And when he heard that it was Jesus the Nazarene, he began to cry out and say: Son of David, have mercy on me!
And many rebuked him, telling him to be silent; but he cried out all the more: "Son of David, have mercy on me!"
Jesus stopped and ordered him to be called. And they called the blind man and said to him: "Do not be afraid; get up, he is calling you."
And he threw off his garment, got up and came to him.
Jesus answered and said to him: What do you want, what shall I do for you? And the blind man said to him: Teacher, that I may open my eyes.
And Jesus said to him: "[?] go; your faith has saved you." And immediately he received his sight and followed him on the road.
And when they drew near to Jerusalem, to Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives, he sent two of the disciples
And he said to them: Go to the village that is before you; and as you enter it you will find a colt tied, on which no one has yet sat. Untie it and bring it to me.
If anyone says anything to you, say: Its lord needs it, and he will send it here immediately.
And they went and found the colt tied at the door, outside at the entrances, and they untied it.
And some of those standing there said to them: What are you doing, that you are untying that colt?
And they told them just as Jesus had commanded them; and they let them go.
And they brought the colt to Jesus and laid garments on it, and he sat upon it.
And many spread their garments on the road, and others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
And those who went ahead of him and those who followed behind cried out and said: Hosanna in the highest! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!
Blessed is the coming of the kingdom of David, our father! Peace in the heavens and glory in the highest!
And he entered Jerusalem, into the temple, and looked around at everything, for the hour was evening. And he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
And on the next day, as they were coming out of Bethany, he became hungry.

And he saw from afar a fig tree that had only leaves on it, and he came to see whether he might find anything on it. And he came to it and found nothing but leaves only, for it was not the season for figs.
And he said to it: Let no one ever again eat fruit from you, forever. And his disciples heard this word.

And Jesus came to Jerusalem, and he entered the temple and began to drive out from the temple those who sold and those who bought; and he scattered the tables of the money-changers and overturned the seats of those who sold doves.
And he would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple.
And he taught and said to them: It is written: My house shall be called a house of prayer by all the nations, but you have made it a den of robbers.
And the chief priests and the scribes heard this, and they sought how they might destroy him; and they were afraid of him, for all the people were astonished at his teaching.
And when it was evening, he went out outside the city.
And as they were passing by at dawn, they saw the fig tree withered from the root.
And Peter remembered and said to him: Teacher, look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered.
Jesus answered and said to them:
Have faith in God! Amen I say to you: whoever says to this mountain, Be uprooted and fall into the sea! and does not doubt in his heart, but believes that what he says will happen, it will be so.
Therefore I say to you: whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you will receive it, and it will be yours.
And when you stand in prayer, forgive, if you remember anything evil against anyone, so that your Father also, who is in heaven, may forgive you your sins.
And they came again to Jerusalem. And as he was walking about in the temple, the chief priests and the scribes and the elders came to him
And they said to him: "By what authority do you do this, and who gave you this authority?"
But Jesus answered and said to them: "I too will ask you one question, and you answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do this.
Was the baptism of John from heaven, or from men? Tell me."
And they reasoned among themselves and said: "If we say, 'It was from heaven,' he will say to us, 'Then why did you not believe him?'
And if we say, 'From men,' we are afraid of the people, for all held John to be a prophet."
And they answered Jesus and said to him: "We do not know." And Jesus answered and said to them: "Neither will I tell you by what authority I do this."
And he began to speak to them in parables: "A certain man planted a vineyard, and put a wall around it, and made a winepress, and built a tower, and gave it to tenant farmers and went away.
And at the time of the fruit he sent a servant to those tenants, so that he might receive the fruit of the vineyard.
But they seized him and beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
Then again he sent another servant to them, and him too they set upon [?] and sent him away disgraced.
And then he sent another, and him they killed; and many others — some they tortured and some they killed.
Last of all, he had one son, his beloved, and he sent him to them, for he said: 'They will respect my son.'
But when those tenants saw him coming to them, they said to one another: 'This is his heir; come, let us kill him, and the inheritance will be ours.'
And they seized him and killed him and threw him out of the vineyard.
Now what will the lord of the vineyard do to them? He will come and destroy those tenants and give the vineyard to others.
Have you not even read this scripture: 'The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner;
this was from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes'?"
And they wanted to seize him, but they feared the people, for they knew that he had spoken that parable against them. And they left him and went away.
And they sent to him some of the Pharisees and the Herodians, to trap him in his words.

And they came and questioned him with guile and said to him: "Teacher, we know that you are truthful and have no concern for anyone, for you do not regard the person of men, but truly teach the way of God. Tell us: is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or should we not pay?"
But he knew their hypocrisy and said to them: "Why do you test me, hypocrites? Bring me a denarius, and let me see it."
And they brought it. And Jesus said to them: "Whose is this image and inscription?" And they said to him: "Caesar's."
Jesus answered and said to them: "Give to Caesar what is Caesar's, and to God what is God's!" And they marveled at this and went away.
And Sadducees came to him, who said that there is no resurrection, and they questioned him and said to him:
"Teacher, Moses wrote thus for us: if someone's brother dies and he has a wife, and no child is left, his brother should take his wife and raise up an heir for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first took a wife and died, and no child was left.
And the second took her and died, and no child was left, and the third likewise,
up to the seventh, and no child was left to him. Last of all, the woman also died.
Now then, in the resurrection, when they rise, whose wife among them will she be, for all seven had her as wife?
Jesus answered and said to them: Is it not for this reason that you err, because you know neither the scripture nor the power of God?
When they rise from the dead, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but they are like the angels in heaven.
But concerning this, that the dead rise, have you not read in the book of Moses, at the bush, how God spoke to him: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob?
He is not the God of the dead, but of the living. But you are greatly mistaken.
And one of the scribes came up to him, as he heard them, how they were disputing the matter with him. He knew that he had answered them well. He too asked him: Which is the first commandment?
And Jesus said to him: First of all is this: Hear, O Israel, the Lord your God, the Lord is one;
and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength. This is the first.
And the second is like it: You shall love your neighbor as yourself. There is no other commandment greater than these.
The scribe said to him: Well said, Teacher; you have spoken truly, that God is one, and there is no other besides him;
And to love him with all the soul and with all the strength and with all the understanding, and to love one's neighbor as oneself: this is greater than all sacrifices and offerings.
And Jesus saw that he had answered wisely, and said to him: You are not far from the kingdom of God. And no one dared to question him any longer.
Jesus answered and said to them, as he was teaching in the temple: How then do the scribes say that the Christ is the son of David?
David himself says by the Holy Spirit: The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I put your enemies beneath your feet.
David himself calls him Lord; so how is he his son? And the great crowd listened to him gladly.
And he said in his teaching: Beware of the scribes, who like to walk about in finery and to be greeted in the streets,
and to sit in the high seats in the synagogue and to sit first in the foremost place at meals.
They devour the houses of widows and for a pretext pray at length; they will receive the greater judgment.
Jesus stood before the treasury and watched how the people were putting copper coins into the treasury. And many rich people put in much.
And a poor widow came and put in two tiny coins, which is a quadrans.
And he called his disciples to him and said to them: Amen I say to you, this poor widow has offered to the treasury more than all of them.
For all of them offered out of their surplus, but she out of her want offered everything she had, her whole livelihood.
And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples said to him: Teacher, look, what stones these are and what a building!
Jesus answered and said: Do you see these very great buildings? Amen I say to you: there shall not be left here a stone upon a stone that shall not be torn down.
And as he sat on the Mount of Olives opposite the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately:
Tell us, when will this be, and what will be the signs when these things are accomplished?
Jesus answered and said to them: "Take heed that no one leads you astray."
For many will come in my name and say: I am the Christ, and they will lead many astray.
When you hear of battles and reports of battles, do not be alarmed, for it must happen, but it is not yet the end.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in place after place, and famines and plagues. All these are the beginning of the pains.
And they will hand you over to councils, and they will torment you in synagogues, and you will stand before rulers and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to all the gentiles.
But first this gospel must be preached.

And when they bring you to hand you over, do not worry beforehand about what you will say, but whatever is given to you in that hour, say that, for it will not be you who are speaking, but the Holy Spirit.
For brother will hand over brother to death, and father his child, and children will rise up against their parents and will kill them.
And you will be hated by all for the sake of my name; but whoever endures will be fully saved.
When you see that abomination of desolation standing where it ought not to be (let the one who reads understand), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains.
And let the one who is on the housetop not come down into the house, nor go in to take anything from his house.
And whoever is out in the field, let him not turn back to take his garment.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days!
But pray that this may not happen in winter.
For those days will be days of tribulation, such as has never happened from the beginning, when God created, until now, nor ever will be.
And if the Lord had not shortened those days, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the elect, whom he has chosen, he has shortened those days.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, here is the Christ,' or 'There he is,' do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will perform signs and wonders, in order to lead astray, if they could, even the elect.
But you, take heed: behold, I have told you everything beforehand.
But in those days, after that affliction, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light;
and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers that are in the heavens will be shaken.
And then they will see the Son of Man coming with power and great glory.
And then he will send out his angels and will gather his elect from the four winds, from the end of the earth to its other end.
Learn this parable from the fig tree: when its branches become tender and the leaf comes out, know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things come to pass, know that it is near, at the doors.
Amen, I say to you: this generation will not pass away until all these things take place.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father alone.
But take heed, be watchful and pray, for you do not know when that time will be.
It is as when a man going on a journey leaves his house and gives his servants his property and authority, and to each one his work, and commanded the doorkeeper to be watchful.
Keep watch, therefore, for you do not know when the lord of the house will come: in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrow, or at dawn.
Lest he come suddenly and find you sleeping.
What I say to you, I say to all: be watchful.
And the Passover, which is the Passion of Unleavened Bread, was after two days. And the chief priests and the scribes were seeking Jesus, how they might seize him by treachery and kill him.
But they said: "Not during this feast, lest there be an uproar among the people."

And as Jesus was in Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper, and he was reclining at table, a woman came who had an alabaster jar of ointment of genuine nard, of great price, and she broke the alabaster jar and poured it on his head.
There were some who were angry among themselves and said, 'Why was this waste of the ointment done?'
'For this could have been sold for more than three hundred drachmas and given to the poor.' And they were angry with her.
But Jesus said to them: "Let her alone; why do you trouble her? For she has done a good deed to me.
For the poor are always with you. If you wish, you may do good to them; but I am not going to be with you always.
What she had, she did: she hastened to anoint my body with ointment; she did it for my burial.
But amen I say to you: wherever this gospel is preached in all the world, what this woman has done will also be told in memory of her.
And Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests in order to hand him over to them.
And when they heard this, they rejoiced and promised to give him silver. And he was seeking how he might hand him over to them at an opportune time.

And on the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they were slaughtering the Passover, his disciples said to Jesus: Where do you wish us to go and prepare for you, so that you may eat this Passover meal?
And he sent two of his disciples and said to them: Go into the city, and when you enter the city a man will meet you who is carrying a jar of water; follow him to wherever he goes in.
Say to the master of the house: The Teacher says: Where is my lodging, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?
And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and prepared; there make ready for us."
And the disciples went out to prepare, and they came to the city and found it just as Jesus had told them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
And when it was evening, he came with the twelve.
And as they sat down and were eating, Jesus said: Amen I say to you: one of you who is eating with me will hand me over.
And they began to be sorrowful and to say to him, one by one: "Surely it is not I?" And another said: "Surely it is not I?"
And Jesus answered and said to them: "One of the Twelve, the one who dips his hand into this dish with me, he will betray me."
The Son of Man indeed goes, as it is written of him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is handed over; it would have been better for him if that man had not been born.
As they were eating, he took bread, blessed it and broke it, and gave it to them and said: Take; this is my body.
And he took the cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, and they all drank from it.
And he said to them: This is my blood of the new covenant, poured out for many.
Amen I say to you: I will no longer drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new in the kingdom of God.
And after they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
And Jesus said to them: You will all stumble because of me this night, for it is written: I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.
But after my resurrection I will go before you to Galilee."
But Peter answered and said to him: Even if all stumble, yet I will never stumble.
Jesus said to him: "Amen, I say to you that today, this night, before the cock crows twice, you will deny me three times."
But Peter spoke all the more insistently: Even if it means my death with you, I will never deny you. -- And likewise they all said the same.
And they came to a village whose name was Gethsemane. And Jesus said to his disciples: Sit here while I pray.
And he took Peter and James and John with him and began to be dismayed and distressed.
And he said to them: "My soul is sorrowful even unto death; stay here and keep watch."
And he went on a little further and fell to the ground and prayed that, if it were possible, that hour might pass from him.
And he said: Abba, my Father, everything is possible for you, even for this cup to pass from me; yet not what I wish, but whatever you wish.
And he came and found them asleep and said to Peter: Simon, are you sleeping? Were you not able to keep watch with me for one hour?
Keep watch and pray, so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak."
And again he went away and prayed, and said the same words.
And he returned again and found them asleep, for their eyes were heavy, and they did not know what word to answer him.
And he came again a third time and said to them: Sleep from now on and rest. The end has arrived, and the hour has come. Behold, the Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of sinners.
Rise, let us go from here. Behold, the one who is handing me over has drawn near.
And while he was speaking, Judas Iscariot came, one of the twelve, and with him a crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
For his betrayer had given them a sign and said to them: "The one I kiss, that is he; seize him and lead him away carefully."
And immediately he approached and said to him: "Rejoice, teacher!" And he kissed him.
And they laid their hands on him and seized him.
And a certain one of those standing by drew a sword and struck the servant of the high priest and cut off his ear.
Jesus answered and said to them: "You have come out with swords and clubs to seize me as if against a robber.
"Day after day I was with you in the temple, and I was teaching you, and you did not seize me; but this is so that the books of the prophets may be fulfilled."
Then all his disciples left him and fled.
And one certain young man alone was following him, and he had wrapped a linen cloth around his naked body. And the other young men seized him.
And he left the linen cloth behind and fled from them naked.
And they led Jesus to Caiaphas, the high priest. And all the chief priests and the scribes and the elders gathered together.
And Peter followed him from afar, as far as inside the courtyard of the high priest, and he sat with the servants and warmed himself before the light of the fire.
And the chief priests and the whole council were seeking witnesses against Jesus, so that they might kill him, and they were not finding any.
For many were bearing false witness against him, and their testimonies were not consistent.
And certain others rose up and bore false witness against him and said:
"We heard him say: 'I will destroy this temple made with hands, and on the third day I will build one not made with hands.'"
And even so their testimonies did not agree.
And the high priest stood up in their midst, questioned Jesus, and said: "Do you answer nothing to what these men testify against you?"
But Jesus remained silent and gave him no word in answer. And then the high priest questioned him a second time and said to him: "Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed One?"
And Jesus answered and said to him: "You say that I am the Christ. And from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the powers and coming with the clouds of heaven."
And the high priest tore his garment and said: "What further need do we have of witnesses?"
"You have all heard the blasphemy from his mouth. What is your will?" Then all condemned him as deserving of death.
And some began to spit in his face and to strike him with their fists, and they said to him: "Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?" And the servants brought him forward to slap him.
And as Peter was in the courtyard, one of the high priest's maidservants came.
And when she saw him warming himself, she looked at him and said: "You too were with Jesus the Nazarene."
But he denied it and said: "I do not know, nor do I understand, what you are saying." And Peter went out to the outer courtyard, and the rooster crowed.
Then the maidservant saw him again and began to say to those standing by: "This man too is one of them."
But he denied it again. And then, after a little while, those standing by said to Peter: "Truly you are one of them, for you are a Galilean."
But Peter began to curse and to swear: "I do not know this man of whom you speak."
And immediately the rooster crowed a second time. And Peter remembered the word that Jesus had said to him: "Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times." And he began to weep.
And immediately it dawned, and the chief priests took counsel with the elders and the scribes and the whole assembly. And they bound Jesus and led him away and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Pilate questioned him and said: "Are you the king of the Jews?" And Jesus answered and said to him: "You have said it."
And the chief priests accused him greatly. And he answered nothing.
And Pilate questioned him again and said: "Do you answer nothing? Look how many things they accuse you of!"
But Jesus answered nothing further, so that Pilate was even greatly amazed.
And at every feast he would release to them one prisoner, whomever they requested.
Now there was a certain Barabbas, bound with the insurgents, who had killed a man in the uprising.
And the people cried out to request him, as he always granted them.
And Pilate answered and said to them: "Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?"
He knew that the chief priests had handed him over out of envy.
But they stirred up the people, so that he would release Barabbas to them.
And Pilate answered again and said to them: "And what shall I do with this king of the Jews?"
But they cried out again, at the instigation of the chief priests, and said: "Crucify him!"
And Pilate said to them: "What evil has he done?" And they cried out all the more and said: "Crucify him!"
And Pilate wished to please the people, and he released Barabbas to them, but he struck Jesus with a whip and handed him over to them to be crucified.
And the soldiers led him into the inner courtyard, which is the praetorium, and they called together the whole company [lit. "kindred"].
And they clothed him in purple and placed on him a woven crown of thorns.
And they began to salute him and to say: "Hail, king of the Jews!"
And they struck him on the head with a reed and spat on him, and they knelt down and bowed down to him.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped the purple from him and clothed him in his own garment and led him out to crucify him.
And they pressed into service a passer-by, a certain Simon of Cyrene, who was coming from the field, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
And they brought him to the place of Golgotha, which translated is the Place of the Skull.
And they offered him wine mixed with myrrh to drink, but he did not take it.
And they crucified him and divided his clothes, casting lots over them to decide who would take what.
Now it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
And the inscription of the charge against him was written thus: "This is the king of the Jews."
And with him they crucified two robbers, one on his right and one on his left.
And then the scripture was fulfilled which says: "He was counted among the lawless."
And those passing by reviled him, shaking their heads and saying: "Aha, you who would destroy the temple and rebuild it on the third day,
save yourself and come down from the cross.
Likewise the chief priests, with the scribes, mocked him among themselves and said: "He saved others; can he not save himself, the Christ, the king of Israel?
Let him come down now from the cross, so that we may see it and believe." And those crucified with him likewise reproached him.
And when it was the sixth hour, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice and said: "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?" which in translation is: "My God, my God, why do you forsake me?"
And some of those standing there before him heard it and said: "Look, he is calling Elijah."
And they ran and filled a sponge with vinegar and put it on a reed and gave him a drink, saying: "Leave him be; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down."
But Jesus cried out with a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And the curtain of the temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.
And when the centurion who stood before him saw that he cried out and gave up his spirit, he said: "Truly this man was the Son of God."
There were also some women watching from afar, among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the Less and of Joses, and Salome,
who had followed him when Jesus was in Galilee, and many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
And as evening was coming on, for it was Friday, which is the day before the Sabbath,
Joseph of Arimathea came, a distinguished councillor, who was also awaiting the kingdom of God; he dared to go in to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.
But Pilate was surprised that he had already died, and he summoned the centurion and asked him whether he had died so soon.
And he learned this from the centurion, and he granted the body to Joseph.
And he bought linen, took him down from the cross, wrapped him in that linen, and laid him in a tomb that had been hewn out of rock; and he rolled a stone and set it against the door of the tomb.
Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were there and saw where they laid him.
And when the Sabbath had passed, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome bought ointment, so that they might go and anoint him.
And very early at dawn on the first day of the week they came to the tomb, just as the sun was rising.
And they were saying to one another: "Who will roll the stone away from the door of the tomb for us?"
And they looked and saw that the stone, which was very large, had been rolled away.
And when they went into the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, dressed in a white garment, and they were alarmed.
But he said to them: "Do not be alarmed! You seek Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified. He has risen; he is not here. Behold the place where they laid him.
But go and tell his disciples and Peter: 'Behold, he is going before you to Galilee; there you will see him, as he told you.'"
And when they heard this, they went out and fled from the tomb, for they were trembling and astonished. And they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.
And he rose at dawn on the first day of the week and appeared first to Mary Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.
She went and told his fellow disciples, who were mourning and weeping.
But when they heard that he was alive and had appeared to her, they did not believe it.
After this he appeared in another form to two of them as they were walking on their way to a village.
And they came and told the others, and they did not believe them either.
Last of all he appeared to the eleven as they sat at table, and he reproached them for their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they had not believed those who had seen him risen.
And he said to them: "Go into all the world and preach this gospel to all creation.
Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, and whoever does not believe will be condemned.
And these signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons, they will speak in new tongues,
they will take hold of serpents, and even if they drink something deadly, it will not harm them in any way; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.
And the Lord, after this speaking to them, was lifted up into heaven and sat at the right hand of God.
And they went out and preached throughout all the earth, with the help of the Lord, and with the confirmation of the word by him, through the signs that followed them.
